title: Capability gap
description: A capability the studio needs and no current agent covers, recorded before anyone proposes hiring for it. This record exists to make workforce growth evidence-driven instead of enthusiastic. ADR-0004 removed headcount as the anti-sprawl control and replaced it with mechanical distinctness checks; ADR-0005 removed the fixed ceiling entirely. What neither supplied was the other half -- a reason a NEW role should exist at all. Without that, 'the roster may grow' becomes 'the roster grows', which is the sprawl the founder forbade in the first place. So: the gap is filed first, with evidence and with the specific reason the existing roster cannot absorb the work; only then may a specialist be proposed; and creation itself remains a constitution edit, which is human-exclusive. Filing this record grants no authority to act on it.

capability.description: The missing capability, stated as work the studio needs done rather than as a job title. 'Nobody maintains the cockpit generator' is a capability; 'we need a tools engineer' is a hire looking for a justification.

signal.description: Which of the recognised gap signals fired. Restricted to a closed set so that 'it would be nice to have' cannot be filed as a gap: every entry here is something observable in the repository or in the record trail.

evidence.description: Records, file paths or commands that substantiate the signal. Same rule as a proposal: a gap with no evidence is an opinion, and the schema refuses it.

consideredExisting.description: The agents examined and rejected as owners, each with the reason. This is the field that stops a duplicate role being created out of ignorance of the roster: the near-duplicate output check catches an overlap after the fact, and this catches it before anyone writes the definition.

whyExistingRosterIsInsufficient.description: Why activating a dormant agent, widening an existing scope or accepting the work as unowned does not answer the gap. Activation is always the cheaper answer and must be ruled out explicitly.

affectedProjects.description: Project ids from Studio/constitution/projects.json. Empty or absent means the gap is in the studio layer itself rather than in any one project.

proposedSpecialist.description: The role that would close the gap. Optional on purpose: a gap is worth recording even when nobody yet knows what would fill it, and forcing a proposal at filing time is how observation turns into hiring.

measurableOutput.description: Must not duplicate any existing agent's. OrgCrossCheckTests enforces that once the agent exists; WorkforceCrossCheckTests enforces it here, while it is still only a proposal and cheap to change.

inputs.description: What the role reads or consumes to do its work.

boundaries.description: What the role may not do. A proposal without stated limits is a request for unbounded authority.

activationCriteria.description: The condition under which the role should start work, in the same observable form as an existing agent's activatesWhen.

status.description: open: recorded, nothing decided. proposed: a specialist has been described and is awaiting the authorisation path. filled: an agent now covers it -- by activation, by widening an existing scope, or by creation. rejected: the gap was examined and judged not worth staffing, which must carry a resolution. superseded: another gap record replaced this one.

resolvedBy.description: The agent id that now covers the capability, once filled.

resolution.description: How it was closed, and by whose authority. Required on anything but open and proposed, so a gap cannot quietly vanish.

decisionId.description: The ADR that authorised creation, where creation was the answer. Creation is a constitution edit and therefore human-ratified; this is the pointer to that ratification.

allOf.description: A gap that claims a specialist has been proposed must actually carry the proposal.
Closing a gap requires saying how. Otherwise the record degrades into a to-do list that gets tidied rather than answered.
A filled gap names the agent that fills it, or nothing was actually filled.
